programs.name: Disabled Vet Exemption

exemptionValue.quote: The first forty-five thousand dollars ($45,000) of appraised value of the residence is excluded from taxation.

survivingSpouse.quote: The surviving spouse of a disabled veteran who has not remarried.

ptRequired.quote: a service-connected, permanent, and total disability

ratingRequired.quote: a service-connected, permanent, and total disability

altQualifier.correct: SAH grant recipients (38 U.S.C. 2101) also qualify regardless of rating

programs.effectiveChanges: None enacted for TY2026 or TY2027. The statute's session-law history still ends at 2010-96 and the current text reads $45,000. 2025-26 bills to raise or replace it were all still in committee on 10/21/26: H118 'Disabled Veterans Tax Relief Bill' (= S228; re-referred to House Rules 9/23/2025), S128 'Heroes Homestead Act' ($76,500; referred to Senate Rules 2/24/2025), H1122 'Expand Disabled Veteran Prop. Tax Exclusion' (full value; referred to House Rules 4/30/2026). None chaptered. The TY2027 Form AV-9 (Web 6-26) is posted and the exclusion remains $45,000 per the filing-layer record.
programs.note: Row is correct on amount and type; only survivingSpouse was wrong (the row's own details text already says the unremarried surviving spouse qualifies, including the spouse of a veteran who died of a service-connected condition or in the line of duty). No income or age test. Eligibility measured Jan 1; apply by June 1; single application.

summary: NC's single row is right at $45,000 of appraised value for 100% P&T (or SAH recipients) and the 2025-26 bills to raise it (H118/S228, S128, H1122) remain unenacted, so nothing changes for TY2026 or TY2027; the only field fix is survivingSpouse to true. Effective rate should drop from 0.84% to about 0.66% (Tax Foundation, 2024 data).
